title: How to Switch from Consensus to Storylane
summary: Moving from Consensus to Storylane? This guide covers how to migrate your demo content, the steps to switch, and what your team gains with interactive demos.
body_markdown:
If you're using Consensus for async video demos and considering a more interactive approach, this guide covers what switching to Storylane looks like: what happens to your existing demo content, the steps to migrate, and what changes after.


## Why teams move from Consensus to Storylane


If you're still evaluating options, Storylane's[full comparison with Consensus](https://www.storylane.io/blog/storylane-vs-consensus) covers features, pricing, and which fits your team.


If you've already decided to move, the most common reasons teams make the switch are:


- **Async video covers one stage, not the full journey.** Consensus built its reputation on delivering video demos asynchronously to buying committees. That works well for mid-funnel nurture. It doesn't cover self-serve product discovery at the top of funnel, live SE demos, sandbox environments, or post-sales onboarding from one platform.
- **Interactive demos require higher-tier access.** Consensus's Simulation capability, which gets closer to interactive product demos, is only available on higher-tier plans. Teams that want interactive demos from their first seat often find themselves buying more than expected to get the core capability they were after.
- **Demo creation is click-heavy and management gets unwieldy.** Reviewers consistently describe building and maintaining Consensus demos as click-intensive, with library management becoming cumbersome as the number of videos and simulations grows.
- **Pricing with no entry point to test.** Consensus starts at $600/month for five seats, billed annually, with no free plan or trial. For teams that want to evaluate with real demos before committing, there's no low-friction way in.
- **The async video advantage is narrowing.** Consensus built a strong position around async video demos for buying committees. That category is commoditizing, and the tools gaining ground offer interactive demos, lead capture, and AI qualification in the same platform.


## What happens to your existing Consensus content?


Consensus videos don't migrate as-is, but your demo content does. Your CSM helps identify which flows matter most, then captures and rebuilds them as interactive Storylane demos from your live product. What comes out is something prospects can actually use, not just watch.


## Step-by-step: switching from Consensus to Storylane


**1. Identify your highest-priority demo content**


List the Consensus videos or simulations currently tied to active pipeline: which ones are sent most frequently, which have the highest watch rates, which appear in your active sales sequences. These are your migration priorities.


**2. Start a Storylane trial or book a migration call**


Sign up at storylane.io or book a demo directly. The migration call is worth it if you have multiple high-use demos: your CSM helps you plan the rebuild sequence and gets your first demos live quickly.


**3. Capture your first interactive demos**


Storylane's browser extension captures your product directly: click through the flow you want to demo and Storylane captures it as an interactive HTML demo. Your CSM adds guided steps, annotations, and branching on top of the capture.


**4. Review and configure with your CSM**


Your CSM walks through the demos with you. This is where you set up[lead capture forms](https://www.storylane.io/blog/lead-forms-in-storylane-capturing-your-most-promising-leads) , configure[CRM routing and viewer identification](https://www.storylane.io/blog/guide-to-lead-attribution-for-interactive-demos) , add persona-specific branching paths, and replace your Consensus send links with Storylane embeds.


**5. Deploy across your full go-to-market stack**


Storylane supports[embedding across your full GTM stack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/product-demos-on-multiple-platforms) : website, email sequences, sales decks, LinkedIn outreach, and review sites like G2. The same demo library serves marketing, sales, and CS rather than sitting in a separate video tool.


## What you gain after switching


- **Demos prospects interact with, not just watch.** Interactive HTML demos let buyers explore your product at their own pace: click through the flow relevant to their use case, revisit a feature, or branch to a different persona path. That engagement depth is what async video can't replicate.
- **Full-funnel coverage from one platform.** Storylane covers top-of-funnel self-serve embeds, mid-funnel personalized demos for buying committees, live SE demos, and sandbox environments. You stop stitching together separate tools for each stage.
- **Lead capture and account-level intelligence.** Know which companies are engaging with your demos, which steps they complete, and where they drop off. Route those signals directly to HubSpot or Salesforce for follow-up on the right accounts at the right time.
- **Branching for different buyer paths.** Build one demo with multiple tracks for different roles, industries, or company sizes.[Demo personalization at this level](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demo-personalization-software) replaces the need for a separate video for every persona.
- **A free trial before you commit.** Storylane lets you start building and testing demos before you sign a contract. You can validate the platform with real demos and real traffic before locking in.


Ready to move your demos over?[Start a free trial](https://app.storylane.io/signup) or[book a migration call](https://www.storylane.io/request-demo) to see how quickly your team can be running interactive demos.
